hook: If Mom Calls Tuesday, Can You Get *Home*?
dek: 10 countries ranked by cost, quality of life and how fast you can get back to New York.

slides.label: The Real Question
slides.text: InterNations and International Living rank countries by cost. We added what they don't: can you get *home by dinner*?

slides.label: Panama #1
slides.text: Panama is #1. It's spent the *US dollar* for over a century, no exchange rate, and 87% of expats say they're happy.

slides.label: Mexico's Catch
slides.text: Mexico is easiest to settle into, but residency got harder: the income bar jumped to about *$4,400 a month* in 2026.

slides.label: DR: Move Home
slides.text: The Dominican Republic isn't in either top 10. It's our pick anyway: *3.5 to 4 hours* home, the shortest flight on the list.

slides.label: Europe Picks
slides.text: Costa Rica is #1 for climate, Portugal wins on value, Spain tops quality of life. All three keep you *under 8 hours* from home.

slides.label: Greece's Trade-off
slides.text: Greece was just named the *best place to retire on Earth*, first time in 35 years. But it's 9 to 10 hours from New York, so it lands 7th here.

slides.label: Cheapest Option
slides.text: Thailand and Malaysia are the cheapest: *$1,200 a month* can cover a full life. The trade is a *20 hour* trip home with no nonstop.

slides.label: Last Word
slides.text: The cheapest country isn't the best one if it puts you a *day away* from the people who need you. Start with the flight home.

question: Which country's on your list: Panama, DR or somewhere else?

caption_instagram:
The best countries to live abroad in 2026 aren't just ranked by cost, they're ranked by the flight home. We looked at InterNations' Expat Insider 2026 and International Living's Global Retirement Index, then added the question neither study asks: if your mother calls on a Tuesday, can you be home by dinner?

Panama tops both lists. It's used the US dollar for over a century, so there's no exchange rate to track, and 87% of expats there call themselves happy. Mexico is easiest to settle into, but its residency bar jumped to about $4,400 a month this year. The Dominican Republic isn't in either top 10, but it's our pick: the shortest flight home on the list, 3.5 to 4 hours.

Greece just got named best place to retire on Earth, but it's 9 to 10 hours away, so it lands 7th here. The cheapest spots, Thailand and Malaysia, put you a full day from home.

Panama tops the list: it's used the US dollar for over a century, so there's no currency risk to model into your runway. Mexico is the easiest to build a life in, but its residency income bar jumped to about $4,400 a month this year, worth knowing before you plan a move.
